procedure_metadata.purpose: Analyze prior MCP plugin implementations from source, extract exact implementation evidence, derive reusable design patterns, and construct a verified internal API without executing untrusted plugin code.

definitions.definition: One source file, class, function, module variable, configuration object, or resource reference whose behavior can be established from source.
A verbatim source span identified by source path, source SHA-256, symbol, and line range.
A repeated implementation relationship or structure supported by at least one exact_code_bit and preferably by multiple independent implementations.
A stable implementation capability abstracted from one or more source-backed functions or patterns and expressed with explicit inputs, outputs, state effects, and failure behavior.
A claim entailed by inspected source text or static bytecode metadata.
A conclusion that combines observations but is not itself literally encoded in one authoritative source.

precedence: Current plugin configuration that resolves runtime entrypoints
Tests associated with the current source
Historical .pyc when current source is absent or historical comparison is the explicit subject
authorities.rule: A lower-precedence source must not override a higher-precedence source without an explicit conflict record.

operations.completion_condition: Every .py member is identified by relative path, size, and SHA-256.
Every parseable Python source has a static symbol/import inventory; parse failures are explicit.
Local import edges and explicit file/resource paths are represented without executing modules.
Every selected reusable symbol has verbatim code, path, source hash, and exact line boundaries.
Every consequential selected unit has at least one explicit implementation role.
Each pattern names supporting source units and distinguishes repetition from one-off implementation.
Current source duplication and known historical cache divergence are not conflated.
Each primitive has a stable name, inputs/outputs, state effects, errors, and source derivation.
Configuration selects fixed primitives and cannot silently become arbitrary code execution.
Transport, configuration, state, transition, persistence, verification, and return contracts are explicit and composable.
Snippet hashes/line spans resolve, generated JSON parses, source coverage is counted, and implementation tests pass where code is executed.
COMPLETE only when all required analysis operations are executed and no known material defect remains.

constraints: Do not import or execute prior plugin modules.
Do not infer runtime necessity from filename alone.
Do not quote reconstructed code as exact code.
Do not let historical .pyc override current source.
Do not label an architectural inference as a source observation.
Do not create configurable arbitrary-code execution when fixed internal primitives suffice.
invariants: Every exact_code_bit retains source path, source SHA-256, symbol, and line range.
Every internal API primitive links to source evidence or is explicitly marked newly designed.
Transport behavior remains separable from domain behavior.
State transitions are explicit where state materially affects execution.
Action evidence and resulting-state evidence remain distinct.
A completion claim requires actual analysis/test records, not the presence of expected output files.

verification_model.source_exactness: Re-extract every snippet from source line span and byte-compare it to the stored snippet.
verification_model.dependency_accuracy: Check every claimed local import target exists or mark it unresolved.
verification_model.pattern_support: Require at least one exact source support; mark cross-plugin generalizations as inference.
verification_model.implementation: Run only newly authored AIChannel code/tests; do not execute untrusted prior plugin code.
